Feature.Description:
Returns the Flex to a known, ready state after an emergency stop, halt, or fault.
Recover performs, in order: acknowledge a released E-stop, fully home the robot, reconcile quarantined tip states from the tip sensors, home the gripper jaw, and fully home any Flex Stacker that lost its position. Steps that need a person (a tip of unknown length, an invalid deck ledger, a disconnected module) are reported instead of guessed.

Command.Description:
Acknowledge a released E-stop without moving the robot.
A Flex keeps a released E-stop latched until it is acknowledged. After acknowledging, the robot still needs a full home (Recover does both).

Raise the gripper straight up to the top of travel, keeping the jaw closed on a held plate.
Use it after a plate hit something while being lowered: only the gripper's vertical axis moves, upwards. Then support the plate by hand and run ReleaseGripperInPlace, or move on to Recover once the plate is safe. Recover is still required afterwards.

Clear every recovery gate that does not need a person.
The front door must be closed and the deck must be safe for the gantry to home. Cancelling Recover halts the robot, so a new Recover is required.

Response.Description: The steps that were performed, in order (empty when nothing was required).

Command.Description:
Open the gripper jaw where it stopped, so a held plate can be taken out before Recover.
Use it after a failed or stopped plate move left a plate in the jaw: a full home lifts the gripper first and opens the jaw only at the top, so the plate would fall. Support the plate by hand first. Only the jaw moves; Recover is still required afterwards.

Property.Description: Subscribe to the steps Recover would perform now and the steps that need a person.

Element.Description: Steps Recover performs by itself, in order (empty when nothing is required).
Steps that need a person before or after Recover.

DefinedExecutionError.Description:
The E-stop is pressed, so recovery cannot start.
Make the robot safe, release the E-stop by twisting it, and run Recover again.

The gripper can only be lifted or released in place while the robot waits for recovery.
These actions are for a plate left in the jaw by a failed or stopped move. When no recovery is pending, use the usual gripper or labware-movement commands. When a recovery is already running, wait for it to finish.

The gripper failed to complete a grip, ungrip, or home-jaw action.
The underlying hardware message is preserved so the failure can be diagnosed.

The shared Flex hardware stayed busy longer than the configured lock timeout.
Another SiLA client, an HTTP/Protocol Engine operation, or a long-running module action currently holds the hardware. Wait for that operation to finish (watch the RobotStatusProvider Status property) and retry, or raise lock_timeout_s in the connector configuration.

The operation was aborted because an emergency stop or halt was issued while it ran.
The robot position is no longer trusted. Clear the cause of the halt, fully re-home the robot, follow the RecoveryGuidance reported by RobotStatusProvider, and then re-issue the operation.

The connector refused the operation because an earlier failure left the robot recovery-gated.
The error message lists the ordered recovery actions (for example a full re-home, TipController.ReconcileTipState, or GripperController.HomeJaw). The same guidance is available at any time from the RobotStatusProvider Status property.

The Flex hardware reported an error that has no more specific defined error.
The message preserves the Opentrons error code, name, and detail so the cause can be diagnosed or reported to vendor support. Inspect the robot, resolve the reported condition, re-home, and retry.

The front door is open, so the robot will not home automatically.
Close the front door, make sure nothing is in the gantry's path, and run Recover again.

Automatic recovery finished, but some steps need a person.
The message lists each remaining action (for example removing a tip of unknown length, reconciling the deck ledger, or reconnecting a module). Complete them and run Recover again; the Status property shows what is still required.

Protocol Engine currently owns the Flex for a prepared or active run.
Read status through the connector as usual, but do not issue an independent SiLA hardware command. Stop the Protocol Engine run, or add the operation at an explicit UNITELABS mutation checkpoint through the controlled run-mutation HTTP endpoint, then retry.

A stall or collision was detected during the move; motion was halted.
Clear any obstruction, then re-home before continuing. The underlying hardware message is preserved to aid diagnosis.

The move was accepted but the robot has silently entered a hardware error state.
A movement command can return without raising while the machine has already entered an error state (for example the E-stop became engaged mid-move). This error surfaces that hidden condition so callers never treat such a move as successful. Clear the fault (release the E-stop), then re-home before continuing. The underlying hardware state is preserved to aid diagnosis.

No pipette is attached to the requested mount.
Attach a Flex pipette, re-scan instruments, and retry the tip operation.

The Flex Stacker is not installed, initialized, or safely closed for this operation.
Confirm the Stacker is mechanically installed, close its hopper door, clear any obstruction, home it if necessary, and retry.

The module did not respond — it may be disconnected or powered off.
Check that the module is connected to the Flex and powered on, then retry.

The module reported an error while carrying out the requested operation.
The underlying driver/module message is preserved to aid recovery (e.g. re-seat labware, check the module's status indicators, or power-cycle it).
